meeting_header:
Date: 2026-03-01
Time: 10:00 AM - 11:15 AM PST
Duration: 75 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (AE), Samira Gupta (SE), Tom Hsu (Sales Enablement), Priya Nair (Product), Maya Thompson (AE), Jordan Lee (AE), Carlos Martinez (AE)
Notes: internal enablement session focused on messaging, competitive positioning, and demo practice. Recording by Fireflies.ai
summary: Internal SE/AE enablement covering messaging pillars (latency/cost/reliability), competitive differentiators vs major cloud APIs and inference vendors, demo run-throughs for hosted vs dedicated vs private scenarios, and objection handling. Several concrete next steps and action items assigned.
transcript:
00:00 Alex Rivera: Okay folks, thanks for joining, we'll run 75 minutes, agenda is messaging, competitive positioning, then two demo runs and a role play. 
00:18 Tom Hsu: Quick housekeeping — recording's on, Fireflies is capturing. If you're on mute, unmute for role-play. 
00:30 Samira Gupta: Start with the messaging pillars I suggested — predictable latency, cost controls, and unified deployment modes. We want all AEs to land the same three bullets. 
00:45 Maya Thompson: Quick question, do we lead with performance or cost in an initial outbound? 
00:52 Alex Rivera: Lead with the customer's pain. For infra-heavy startups it's latency and throughput; for enterprise it's security and governance. But default message: "production-grade inference with predictable economics." 
01:10 Jordan Lee: Got it. Can we get a one-liner for openers? Something short for cold outreach. 
01:20 Alex Rivera: "Redwood Inference: predictable, production-grade LLM serving — fast, cost-efficient, and deployable anywhere." Keep it tight. 
01:35 Samira Gupta: Competitive positioning — avoid name-shaming, focus on where we win: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, cost controls (batching, caching recommendations), and observability. Use customer stories not feature lists. 
01:55 Carlos Martinez: People ask about OpenAI pricing — how much should we call out public API price differences? 
02:05 Priya Nair: Use relative examples: "with Redwood's batching and KV-cache we typically see X–Y% lower per-token costs for chat workloads versus public APIs at scale" — avoid specific numbers in cold outreach, but have benchmark doc ready for deeper conversations. 
02:30 Samira Gupta: Let's move to demo script. We have two flows: 1) Hosted API quickstart for product teams; 2) Dedicated/Private for enterprise security/throughput asks. We'll role-play both. 
02:50 Alex Rivera: For hosted demo emphasize: 2 minute setup, model catalog, streaming, function calling, and quick latency demo. For dedicated, emphasize reserved capacity, autoscaling policies, and SLA. For private, emphasize VPC, KMS, and audit logs. 
03:15 Tom Hsu: Practice note — call out fallbacks: if Dedicated capacity is constrained we route to a compatible variant and show the rollback policy in the Console. That resonates with platform teams. 
03:40 Role-play 1: Hosted demo (Alex as AE, Maya as customer) 
03:45 Maya Thompson (as customer): We're a small app team, want low setup friction and pay-as-you-go. How do you compare to OpenAI? 
03:55 Alex Rivera: Short answer: easy to start (hosted API) and scale to predictable costs with dedicated or private as you grow; we surface per-route token cost and latency in the Console so engineering leaders can optimize. 
04:15 Maya (customer): We care about hallucinations — what guardrails do you offer? 
04:20 Samira Gupta (SE): We recommend eval suites tied to PR/CI, structured outputs, function calling enforcement, and quality monitoring in Redwood Optimize for regression alerts. 
04:40 Jordan Lee (interruption): Do we call out fine-tuning or recommend customer use LLM provider fine-tunes? 
04:45 Priya Nair: Put fine-tuning as part of model selection — some customers use open-model fine-tunes, others rely on prompt engineering and retrieval augmented generation. We should avoid committing on managed fine-tuning unless product supports it for that sale. 
05:05 Alex Rivera: Good. Now demo — Samira, can you run the hosted quickstart CLI and show streaming? 
05:10 Samira Gupta: Sure — opening terminal, curl to /v1/generate, passing model=redwood-v2-small, streaming enabled... (typing noises) streaming chunk 1... chunk 2... latency ~120 ms in region us-west-2 — note: these are synthetic numbers for demo. 
06:00 Maya (customer): Nice, but customers will ask about throughput for conversational workloads. 
06:05 Samira Gupta: Mention batching and continuous KV cache; show Console plot of tokens/sec. 
06:20 Alex Rivera: Now switch to dedicated scenario — Jordan will play Security Lead. 
06:25 Jordan Lee (as Security Lead): We need SOC2 compliance and KMS integration. Also data residency in EU. 
06:35 Samira Gupta: We support SOC 2 and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management in Private deployments. For residency we can pin region and provide audit logs via Redwood Console. 
06:55 Jordan (customer): What about network controls? 
07:00 Priya Nair: VPC peering, private control plane, and optional on-prem package for air-gapped environments. Show slide with network topology. 
07:20 Carlos Martinez: In objections we always get "what about model accuracy vs Anthropic/OpenAI?" How do we handle that? 
07:30 Samira Gupta: Emphasize model choice and evaluation — we onboard open models and provide Redwood-verified performance profiles. For high-accuracy needs recommend a larger variant or a verified variant, and offer to run a short benchmark on customer prompts. 
07:50 Alex Rivera: Demo two — show Canary rollout and automatic fallback policy briefly. 
07:58 Samira Gupta: In Console, select model version, create canary rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on quality regressions; show tracing hooks and token-level cost break down. 
08:25 Tom Hsu: Good callout. Now let's practice price objections. Role-play 2 (Carlos as procurement). 
08:30 Carlos Martinez (as Procurement): Your per-token is higher than public APIs — why pay Redwood? 
08:38 Alex Rivera: Because we reduce total unit cost operationally via batching, caching, and routing; plus you get predictable capacity (Dedicated) and enterprise controls — when you factor in SRE overhead and tail latency mitigation, Redwood is often cheaper at scale. Offer to run a TCO comparison with their usage profile. 
09:05 Carlos (procurement): They will ask for hard numbers. 
09:10 Alex Rivera: Right — have the spreadsheet ready but only after NDA or in sales-assisted conversations. For inbound qualified leads, send the benchmark spreadsheet. 
09:25 Maya Thompson: A quick note on partner mentions — if they mention vendors like Replicate or Lambda Labs, the play is: those are infra + model bundles, Redwood is a unified runtime and opinions for production economics. 
09:45 Priya Nair: Another messaging nuance: when talking to platform teams use terms like "KV cache", "continuous batching", "smart routing", and "observability/tracing hooks". For product teams use outcomes: "faster responses, lower bill, predictable SLOs." 
10:05 Samira Gupta: Ok, run-through of the new demo script v1 — call out required slides: 1) quick intro, 2) hosted quickstart live demo, 3) dedicated architecture and SLA, 4) private deployment and security, 5) pricing and next steps. 
10:25 Alex Rivera: We'll do timed practice: aim hosted demo to 6 minutes, dedicated deep dive to 12 minutes. Use Benchmarks doc link in chat when asked. 
10:40 Role-play — rapid-fire objections from the AEs (Jordan, Carlos, Maya) while Samira practices ad-libbing. 
11:00 Samira Gupta: (on the fly) If latency is the concern, we can show percentile latency graphs and explain fallback policies. If cost is concern, show batching, caching, and quantization options. If security, show KMS and audit logs. 
11:25 Jordan Lee: One sticky objection: "We can't send PII to third-party APIs." How tight do we have to be here? 
11:35 Priya Nair: For regulated data we push Private deployment or on-prem. Also emphasize data retention controls and allow customers to opt-out of logging. Have the security pack ready to share. 
11:55 Alex Rivera: Wrapping up — recap action items and next steps. Samira will push demo script v2, Alex shares pricing and Dedicated SKU doc, Tom records the quick pitch. We'll schedule follow-up role-play next week. 
12:10 Tom Hsu: Thanks everyone — session ends.

Note: Transcript has occasional ASR errors (proper names and acronyms), filler words, and overlaps typical of Fireflies exports.
